legend.summary: A scan line moves west to east across NASA's map of how much warmer or cooler than normal the sea is, one map a month: each month of 2025, then the same month of 2026.
legend.method: Only what is under the scan line plays. Where the sea is much warmer than normal, a rising pair of notes rings; where it is much cooler, a low cello falls. North rings higher and in your left ear, south lower and in your right. A deep hum grows with how far from normal the sea under the line is, warm or cool, and is silent over land. Listen for the middle of the Pacific: in 2026, El Niño warms it.

items.meaning: Sea at least 1.2 degrees C warmer than normal for the time of year. A pair from 2 degrees. Louder = warmer.
Sea at least 1.2 degrees C cooler than normal. Louder = cooler.
How far from normal the sea under the line is, warm or cool. Silent over land and sea ice.

legend.caveat: Each map is the average of every daily map NASA made that month (November 2026: 1 to 4 November, the end of NASA's film). Values are read from NASA's colour bar, -4 to +4 degrees C, so anything beyond reads as 4. Normal means the average for that day of the year.

about.what: NASA's map of how much warmer or cooler than normal the sea surface is, one map a month: each month of 2025, then the same month of 2026.
about.who: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio, from the MUR sea surface temperature data of NASA JPL's PO.DAAC.
about.when: January to November 2025, each month followed by the same month of 2026.
about.where: The world ocean. El Niño shows in the central and eastern tropical Pacific.
about.why: El Niño warms the tropical Pacific and shifts heat and rain around the world. Hearing a month of 2025 next to the same month of 2026 makes the change stand out.
about.how: A scan line crosses each map west to east. A rising pair of notes rings where the sea is much warmer than normal, a low cello falls where it is much cooler, and a deep hum grows with how far from normal the sea under the line is.

journey.title: Satellites

frames.alt: NASA's map of sea surface temperature anomaly, January 2025, averaged over 31 days: red where the sea is warmer than normal for the time of year, blue where it is cooler, grey land.
frames.text: January 2025. The El Niño box in the central Pacific is 0.6 degrees C cooler than normal, and 1.0 degrees C cooler than the tropical ocean as a whole: below the El Niño line of 0.5 degrees warmer. Warmest: around 35 degrees south, 145 degrees west; around 35 degrees south, 85 degrees west; and around 25 degrees south, 55 degrees east. Coolest: around 35 degrees south, 115 degrees west; around 65 degrees north, 55 degrees west; and around 5 degrees south, 165 degrees west. 31 percent of the sea read is at least 1 degree warmer than normal, 1 percent at least 1 degree cooler.
